name: Yimas
catalog_quote: Yimas stress is essentially predictable by a simple rule: assign primary stress to the first syllable of the word, and secondary stress to the third syllable, if the word is longer than three syllables. Stress is not phonemic. (Foley 1991:75)

audit.recode_to: no reclassification now. If Foley 1991:75-80 (or Peng 2013's reproduction of his data) shows alternating secondaries in 6+-syllable words, n=6-8 would change 101000/1010000/10100000 -> 101010/1010100/10101010 and 'kind' fixed-strict -> binary iterative (trochaic L-to-R, non-degenerate); n=2-5 cells (10, 100, 1010, 10100) are secure either way.
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: the deciding text is the StressTyp2 entry(Foley 1991:75), confirmed verbatim in the held together with passage 2079 and 12 stress-marked word forms; Foley 1991 itself is not yet obtained, so the check stops at the database transcription. (2) Source: the classification ultimately rests on the right work (Foley 1991, the sole reference grammar; no phonology article, dissertation or instrumental study of Yimas prosody exists per Glottolog's single descriptive ref, the 2026-08-18 lit review search, and archive.org/OpenLibrary/ROA checks now), but only second-hand: a survey excerpt, a course blog, and now Alderete 1999. (3) What the held and downloaded material shows: every channel agrees on n=2-5 (initial primary; trisyllables 100 per Foley's 'if the word is longer than three syllables', StressTyp2 forms ˈawtmayŋi/ˈyamparan, Alderete fn. 8; 4-syll 1010 wúratàkay; 5-syll 10100 mámantàkarman

sources.quote: 'In Yimas, the main stress regularly falls on the initial syllable of a word (3a).
